drapeaux.note: Langue d'origine : danois (orthographe dano-norvégienne de l'époque) ; auteur : Edvard Munch. Laissée telle quelle ; la glose anglaise « Can only have been painted by a madman! » figure dans contenu_vulgarise.

titre: The Scream bears an insult, written by Munch himself
accroche: A pencil graffito calls the author of The Scream a madman. At first a vandal was suspected; in 2021, the Oslo museum recognizes the painter's own handwriting.
contenu_vulgarise:
In the upper left corner of *The Scream*, 1893 version, a line is traced in pencil: “Kan kun være malet af en gal Mand!”, that is, “Can only have been painted by a madman!” It was first assumed that an offended viewer had scribbled it to deface the painting, and its origin remained uncertain: vandalism, or Munch himself.

The inscription is noticed in 1904, eleven years after the painting, when the work is exhibited in Copenhagen, and it is then assumed that an outraged visitor left his verdict. The painting exists in four versions, and only one bears this line.

## Who wrote this sentence?

In February 2021, the National Museum of Norway, in Oslo, announces that the question is settled. The curators analyze the handwriting under infrared, compare it with Munch's notes and letters, and relate it to the circumstances of the painting's first public showing, in 1895. Their conclusion, formulated by the curator Mai Britt Guleng: the handwriting is, without any doubt, Munch's. The museum's director, Karin Hindsbo, draws a broader lesson: we will never be done with Munch's art.

The museum also proposes a date and a context. The painting is shown in Kristiania, present-day Oslo, in 1895. The reception is harsh, and people speculate about his mental health: a medical student, Johan Scharffenberg, asserts at a debate evening that Munch's paintings prove he is not entirely sane. According to the museum, Munch probably added the inscription in 1895 or shortly after, in response to the judgment passed on his work. He was deeply hurt by these accusations and returned to the episode several times in his letters and diary. The museum is categorical about the hand, more cautious about the period (“probably” 1895), and says nothing of the intention.

## A sentence in the artist's own hand

The shift comes down to the direction of the arrow. What was suspected to be an aggression from outside is, according to the museum, a gesture by the artist, placed on his own work after the fact. The sentence ceases to be damage to be repaired and becomes a document on how Munch experienced the reception of his work. One can read in it, and this is a reading by this card, not a conclusion of the museum, the verdict of his detractors copied out by the one who had received it. A line that might have been judged foreign to the painting is part of it, since its author put it there.

What remains is what the infrared does not say: the precise day the pencil touched the painting.

citation.texte: Kan kun være malet af en gal Mand!
citation.source: Pencil inscription on The Scream (1893 version), attributed to Munch by the Nasjonalmuseet in 2021; original text recorded by Scientific American, 2021

carte.punch: The insult written on The Scream would be in Munch's own hand, not a vandal's.
carte.idee: On the 1893 version of The Scream, a pencil sentence says the author must be mad. First attributed to a visitor, it is attributed in 2021 to Munch himself by the Oslo museum, after infrared imaging and comparison with his letters.

quiz.question: What made it possible to conclude that the inscription on The Scream is not the work of a visitor?
choix: A chemical analysis of the pencil, which proves that it dates from 1904
A testimony from Munch's family, published in 2021
Infrared and comparison with his letters
The confession of a visitor identified in the Copenhagen archives
quiz.explication: The museum analyzed the handwriting under infrared, then compared it with Munch's notes and letters. The inscription postdates the painting, probably from 1895 or shortly after. The press release mentions neither a family testimony nor a confession by a visitor.

quiz_supplementaire.question: When is the inscription on The Scream first noticed, and under what circumstances?
choix: In 1904, when the painting is exhibited in Copenhagen, eleven years after it was painted
In 1893, the very day Munch finishes the painting
In 1971, during a preventive restoration of the painting
In 2021, during the infrared analysis carried out by the Oslo museum
quiz_supplementaire.explication: According to Scientific American, the inscription is noticed in 1904 when the painting is exhibited in Copenhagen, eleven years after Munch painted it, and is first attributed to an outraged visitor, not to the artist himself.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Who, at a debate evening in 1895, publicly asserts that Munch's paintings prove he is not entirely sane?
choix: Karin Hindsbo, director of the Oslo museum
Mai Britt Guleng, curator at the museum
A critic from the newspaper Le Figaro
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The Nasjonalmuseet's press release (2021) names Johan Scharffenberg, a medical student, who made these remarks at a debate evening. Hindsbo and Guleng are quoted about the attribution of the handwriting, not about this 1895 episode.
